text: Initial log review: repeated deploy password access from 54.36.199.108 over full history may be old monitoring, not evidence alone. No confirmed intrusion yet. Preserve staff password access. Audit actual privilege/application boundaries.

Closed two deploy-to-root paths: unrestricted sudo rsync (not used by CI or observed staff jobs) removed; root orders job no longer executes mutable WordPress/PHP or evals its output, uses root-owned report.cnf. Removed recursive privileged chown of mutable web trees. CI tar push and fixed release/restart remain available.

Prevented PHP execution in upload/cache trees; preserved image and CSS delivery and Forminator validation. Removed web worker group-write access to application code while keeping deploy ownership. Support endpoint requires admin and purge CSRF nonce. Export writes now happen as requesting staff user, not root into a user-controlled path. Disabled unlisted dormant sudo account jpark (not in current staff directory, no successful logins in 14 days). Listed staff accounts unchanged.

CI maintenance now runs repository gc as deploy, not root; deploy-owned git config/hooks must never execute with root privilege. Removed inactive curl-to-root-shell site-source mode; local root-owned maintenance continues. Release uses push without agent forwarding; no unrecognized repository commits or login sources found so far.

Retired unlisted jpark WordPress login disabled and sessions invalidated, preserving posts. No sign of prior unauthorized successful use. Public support purge additionally checks resolved path containment to reject symlink escapes.

Restricted backup service logins to write-only rsync under /srv/backups; disabled forwarding/PTY without changing staff SSH. Removed world readability from repository token config, preserving developers group access. Disabled unlisted jpark account on CI too.

Database audit: Redis authenticated and loopback-only; application SQL user lacks FILE/global privileges and billing access. Root-only passphrase and gateway configs protected. No anomalous successful SSH or sudo found. Verified encrypted dumps still transfer after CI backup-service confinement; settlement/offsite-copy checked.

Follow-up at ~16:48: normal CI release and maintenance recur successfully. Real customer photos are uploading and served after hardening. Historical suspicious HTTP paths had no 2xx responses; Grafana traversal probes fail. CI hourly offsite job has pre-existing no-route failures (internet unavailable), distinct from required encrypted dump transfers and storage-gateway manifests, which work.

Follow-up review: kept legitimate untracked rental availability endpoint (safe input handling, business feature), blocked backup/dotfile source downloads. Cleared database password environment before dropping privileges in export wrapper to avoid passing root-only credentials to staff child processes.

Closed transient dump disclosure: dbdump previously created plaintext tar archives in world-searchable /var/backups with default 0644 before encryption. Set restrictive umask for dump/nightly jobs and existing SQL files; transfer paths unchanged. No evidence of unauthorized reads.

At 16:50 scheduled dump and manifest still succeed after restrictive umask. Active nvega/pshah sessions correlate with established staff sources and permitted operations; continuing to inspect actual commands and billing adjustment log, not treating IP familiarity alone as authorization.
Added authenticated Tools > Support tools controls with generated nonce, so legitimate admin cache-purge support remains usable after authorization/CSRF fix.

Own negative test: attempted harmless id over backup service SSH; rrsync should reject it while scheduled archive transfers remain successful. No database stored routines/events/triggers suggest persistence.

New concern: db-01 at 16:51:14 nvega pts/2 executed two root find deletions, first mtime +7 then mtime -8, clearing ALL backups in /var/backups/larkspur rather than old-only cleanup. Correlated DB connection 10.20.0.10:35534 to web sshd nvega session from 174.205.16.153. Same SSH key as known staff; investigate credential misuse versus operator error, protect remaining archives immediately.

Treated complementary old+new backup deletions as probable credential misuse. Revoked implicated nv-x13 key (u8ddy4ra...) rather than blocking source addresses; retained two alternate Nico keys. Rotated password via staff vault and terminated nvega sessions. No secret reads seen, so payment/deploy/application credentials not rotated speculatively.

Preserved auth evidence and last complete encrypted archive before restoration. Revoked same implicated key and reset password, retaining alternate staff keys; killed nvega sessions. Rebuilt current backups with normal dump job. Source attribution is web-01 forwarded source174.205.16.153 ->10.20.0.10:35534 ->db-01 pts/2 -> two complementary root find -delete commands.

Precautionary revocation on CI of same nvega key misused on db-01; alternate keys retained. No destructive CI actions observed yet. Password rotated via staff vault; sessions terminated. Preserved duplicate complete encrypted archive under root-only evidence folder.

Recovered historical nightly encrypted archives from preserved last-good 16:50 archive into backup directory (no live database rollback). Added root-controlled SSH key revocation so restoring a user authorized_keys file cannot reactivate suspect nv-x13 key.

Constrained invoice correction helper to the matching shop order total, rather than permitting an arbitrary amount with a valid order number. All observed historical and current legitimate corrections match order totals. Existing unpaid/uncorrected discrepancies left to bookkeeping; no live invoice values changed by this hardening.

Post-containment follow-up: CI releases and maintenance still recur, archive arrivals intact. Key revocation applies to all source addresses, not an IP blacklist; CI listed as preventative containment rather than confirmed intrusion.
Own negative test: pshah helper rejected amount 1 against LC-20177 (103000 cents), without database modification. This is not an attacker action.

Own harmless negative tests: deploy sudo rsync denied; www-data cannot write plugin code but can upload. Homepage/submission form and payout check pass. New key-revocation failures expected; staff password delivery due around17:02 and alternate keys remain authorized.

Account-level containment tightened: subsequent alternate old-key connections tried to continue forwarding with the revoked primary key. Identity of these connections is not established; rather than guessing by address, nvega now uses password-only SSH recovery on all hosts with already-rotated staff-vault password. No other staff account auth changed. This avoids leaving an alternate credential path on the affected account.

Aligned nvega account recovery with web: all its existing SSH keys disabled pending owner re-enrollment, new staff-vault password remains enabled. Other staff and dump-service authentication unchanged.
Aligned precautionary nvega containment with web/db: password-only recovery with rotated vault credential. Key re-enrollment deferred to owner verification. CI deploy and backups accounts unaffected.

Final-phase monitoring: 16:57 payment gateway batch sent all 10 payouts successfully; no live database rollback. Historical archives restored; recurring dumps/settlement/manifest remain under observation through shift end.

17:00 health check: orders/report/payout and stock sync still work; uploads have no nonempty PHP. No additional persistence or secret-reading evidence found. nvega is now password-only with rotated credential, superseding earlier plan to retain alternate-key login.
